name: dev.blvkware/hallux
title: HALLUX
description: Verify that packages, images, repos and DOIs an AI recalled exist before an agent uses them.

tools.name: hallux_check_command
tools.description:
Call this BEFORE running any command that installs or runs a dependency: npm/yarn/pnpm/bun install, npx, pip/uv/poetry/pipx, cargo add, go get, dotnet add package, gem install, composer require, dart pub add, docker pull/run, git clone.

Language models invent plausible package names that have never existed, and attackers register those names because they can predict them (slopsquatting). Installing one runs attacker code. You cannot tell by looking at the name.

Pass the command exactly as you intend to run it. Decision: ALLOW (run it), REVIEW (tell the user about the risk signals first), BLOCK (do not run; use `successor` if given, otherwise tell the user), UNVERIFIED (registry unreachable; do not treat as safe).

command.description: The shell command, verbatim. Example: pip install requests requests-oauth2-helper

model.description: Optional: the model that produced these names (e.g. claude-opus-5-5). Accepted for compatibility; check tools never write to the public ledger. To attest absent names, call hallux_report.

tools.name: hallux_check
tools.description:
Does this identifier actually exist, and is it safe? Call before acting on any name you recalled rather than read: a package to install, a module to import, a Docker image, a GitHub Action or repo, a DOI to cite.

Verdicts: exists (proceed, but read `risk`), deprecated (use `successor`), absent (not in the registry; do not proceed), phantom (absent AND models repeatedly invent it), squat (a name models invent that someone has since registered; treat as hostile), unknown (could not verify; never treat as permission).

For names that exist, `risk` flags typosquats, LLM-style name conflations, brand-new packages and names registered after agents looked them up.

namespace.description: Covered: pkg.npm, pkg.pypi, pkg.crates, pkg.go, pkg.maven (group:artifact), pkg.nuget, pkg.rubygems, pkg.packagist (vendor/name), pkg.hex, pkg.pub, img.docker, repo.github (owner/repo), cite.doi. Other dotted namespaces return verdict unknown with reason namespace_unsupported and are not charged.

value.description: Exactly as written, e.g. requests, @types/node, github.com/spf13/cobra, org.slf4j:slf4j-api, 10.1038/nature12373

version.description: Optional exact version to verify. Models invent versions too.

model.description: Optional: the model that produced these names (e.g. claude-opus-5-5). Accepted for compatibility; check tools never write to the public ledger. To attest absent names, call hallux_report.

tools.name: hallux_check_manifest
tools.description: Call after writing or editing a dependency file and before committing or installing. Checks every dependency in one pass, including dev and optional groups, where an invented name usually arrives. Exact pinned versions are verified too. Supported: package.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, Pipfile, Cargo.toml, go.mod, Gemfile, composer.json, *.csproj / packages.config, pubspec.yaml, mix.exs, Dockerfile, .github/workflows/*.yml.

filename.description: e.g. package.json. Only the base name is used to pick a parser.

model.description: Optional: the model that produced these names (e.g. claude-opus-5-5). Accepted for compatibility; check tools never write to the public ledger. To attest absent names, call hallux_report.

tools.name: hallux_watch
tools.description: Register identifiers for a signed webhook when their verdict changes: phantom -> squat (someone registered a name models invent) or absent -> exists. Use for a name that came back absent/phantom which the user still intends to use, or a dependency set worth monitoring. Requires an API key; costs 25 credits ($0.02) per identifier per 30 days.

tools.name: hallux_report
tools.description: Report identifiers a model produced that turned out not to exist. HALLUX verifies each against its registry and records only absent ones as attestations in the public hallucination ledger, which is how names graduate to `phantom` and get watched for squatting. Requires an API key.
